title: List graphics and network hardware
summary: Show the graphics card and network adapters that Linux sees on the PCI bus. This only reads hardware information and changes nothing.

aliases.text: which graphics card do I have linux
what wi-fi chip is in my laptop linux
какая видеокарта стоит в компьютере linux
какой wifi адаптер в ноутбуке linux

prerequisites: The lspci command, which comes from the pciutils package (installed by default on most desktops)

steps.explain: List PCI devices, keeping only graphics (VGA, 3D controller) and network (Ethernet, Network controller) lines. Wi-Fi adapters are usually 'Network controller'.

alternatives.explain: Show every PCI device, not only graphics and network ones.
Show the full list with the kernel driver in use under each device.

steps.expect: One line per device, for example '00:02.0 VGA compatible controller: ...' and '02:00.0 Network controller: ...'. Empty output means no matching PCI device was found.

steps.explain: Check which kernel driver is attached to the graphics and network devices. A line 'Kernel driver in use: <DRIVER>' under a device means a driver is loaded for it. If that line is missing, the system has no driver bound to the device.
steps.expect: Device lines followed by 'Kernel driver in use: ...' and 'Kernel modules: ...' lines, for example 'Kernel driver in use: i915'.

verify.expect: Same device list as the previous step, with driver lines.

source.title: lspci manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
